newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU farm reform urgently needed, think tank says.
newsitem.headline: EU farm reform urgently needed, think tank says.

text.p: European Union agricultural policy needs far-reaching and urgent reform to prepare for the next round of world trade talks and EU expansion eastwards, the Centre for European Policy Studies said in a report on Friday.

"The forthcoming WTO trade negotiations on agriculture will add pressure on the EU to open its markets and reduce import and export tariffs," Aart de Zeeuw, chairman of the report's working party, said in a statement.
"The enlargement of the EU to the East will hasten the need for CAP reform," added De Zeeuw, who chaired the GATT agricultural committee during the Uruguay Round negotiations.
The Brussels-based group's report called for EU farmers to be more market-oriented so that they can become more competitive on domestic and world markets.
It also called for a coherent programme to bring EU farm support prices down to world levels according to an agreed timetable and encourage farmers to export without subsidies.
Supply controls, such as set-aside, should be abolished and aid payments to farmers should be linked to measures to protect the environment, the report recommended.
